sources.researchNote: The Boston Public Library dates the card to about 1930–1945, the span of Tichnor’s linen-finish cards. The back prints the hotel’s own advertisement, “Culver Hotel, ‘A Family Hotel!’, Washington at Culver Blvd.”, with the Tichnor Art Company imprint and no copyright notice.

media.title: Culver Hotel, Culver City — Tichnor postcard, c. 1930–1945
media.description: Linen-finish picture postcard of the Culver Hotel, opened in 1924 at Washington and Culver Boulevards in Culver City, the town in which Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer had its studio on Washington Boulevard. It was published by Tichnor Brothers of Boston through its Los Angeles office, the Tichnor Art Company, as card 78506; the back advertises the hotel as “A Family Hotel!”.
media.altText: Coloured postcard of a six-storey red-brick hotel on a street corner, with a rooftop sign reading Hotel Culver City and cars parked in front.
media.publicCaption: The Culver Hotel, Culver City, on a Tichnor postcard of about 1930–1945. MGM’s studio stood on the same boulevard.
media.publicCreditLine: Tichnor Brothers, Boston (Tichnor Art Company, Los Angeles), card 78506; Boston Public Library, Tichnor Brothers Postcard Collection; via Digital Commonwealth.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. Tichnor Brothers of Boston published the card in the United States between about 1930 and 1945, and neither side carries a copyright notice; a work published in the United States before 1978 without notice entered the public domain on publication. The Boston Public Library, which holds the card, records no known copyright restrictions.

places.publicNote: Culver City is the location of the MGM studios where Kaper worked during his Hollywood career.
